overrideReason: Attempt 3's live integration tests (added correctly, unlike attempts 1-2 which had no live coverage at all) initially showed 3 failures out of 7. Investigated each directly rather than assuming the production code was at fault: (1) test_live_okx_candle_backfill_seed_matches_project_calculation_at_historical_bar failed with obtained=2440.0134423037234 vs expected=2324.7957086491806 - a large, real-looking discrepancy. Independently recomputed MACD from scratch (fresh raw OKX candle fetch, manual 250-bar window slicing, direct talib.MACD call, entirely outside both the production code path and the test's own reconstruction) and got 2440.0134423037234 - an EXACT match to the production backfill's own value. This proved the production code is correct and the test's own expected value was wrong. Root cause: the test's pagination cursor added an extra +1 day (`returned.source_timestamp + timedelta(days=1)`) when reconstructing the comparison window, shifting the whole 250-bar window one day too new relative to what the backfill actually used. Fixed the test's cursor to use `returned.source_timestamp` directly. (2) test_live_okx_rubik_rejects_or_fails_to_commit_to_1dutc_period failed because it called response.raise_for_status() unconditionally - OKX's real, expected answer to period=1Dutc on the rubik endpoints is an HTTP 400 (confirmed live), which is itself the finding the test exists to capture (no UTC-aligned bar option exists for long/short ratio and taker volume, confirming period=1D plus disclosure is the correct approach), but raise_for_status() crashed before that could be asserted. Fixed to only inspect the response body on a successful response, treating a non-2xx status as itself the expected rejection. (3) test_live_okx_run_backfill_persists_real_rows_cross_checked_against_fresh_vendor_read[btc_open_interest] failed on a pytest.approx(abs=1e-9, rel=0.0) comparison of two values agreeing to ~15 significant figures at a magnitude of ~2 billion (open-interest USD) - below float64's own representable precision at that magnitude, making the assertion guaranteed-flaky regardless of data correctness. Fixed to rel=1e-9, abs=0.0, which scales correctly across every parametrized case's real magnitude (ratios near 1 through USD values in the billions). After fixing all three, a fourth, previously-unseen failure appeared on re-run: the btc_funding_rate parametrized case raised StopIteration (the fresh comparison fetch did not contain the persisted oldest row's timestamp). Investigated directly rather than assuming another test bug: an isolated diagnostic script running the exact same backfill-then-fresh-fetch sequence showed a PERFECT match (persisted oldest timestamp 2026-06-22 08:00 UTC exactly equal to a fresh fetch's oldest fundingTime), and a subsequent isolated re-run of just that parametrized test case passed cleanly (133.75s, 1 passed). This confirms the StopIteration was a one-off transient OKX API flake (e.g. a momentarily truncated or delayed response), not a reproducible defect in either the production code or the test - it did not recur on either of two independent follow-up checks. Full local suite verified clean on current HEAD: uv run mypy ingest --strict clean, uv run ruff check clean, uv run pytest -q -m "not integration" 374 passed, npm --prefix web run typecheck clean, npm --prefix web test 55/55 passed.

results.note: backfill_okx_candle_indicator (ingest/fetchers/okx.py) sizes its seed window via _backfill_seed_bars, using max(required_bars, lookback*RECURSIVE_SEED_MULTIPLE+1) - for MACD(12,26,9) this correctly resolves to the full 250-bar required_bars window, matching the live pipeline's own contract.

tests/test_backfill_okx.py::test_live_okx_candle_backfill_seed_matches_project_calculation_at_historical_bar, after fixing its own off-by-one pagination cursor, PASSED against the real live OKX endpoint - independently reconfirmed by a from-scratch recomputation outside both code paths, which matched the production value exactly (2440.0134423037234).

backfill_okx_funding_rate persists exactly one vendor-bounded page (limit=100, before=1, ~3 months per research), with source_field explicitly stating 'vendor-bounded backfill page, no synthetic earlier rows'. The live cross-check test passed on retry (see overrideReason for the transient-flake investigation), confirming the persisted earliest date matches a fresh direct read of the same endpoint.

backfill_okx_open_interest reads from open-interest-history (confirmed by direct code review and the passing live cross-check test), and its persisted endpoint/source_field are distinct from the live public/open-interest snapshot's, confirmed by tests/test_backfill_okx.py's offline provenance assertions.

Long/short ratio and taker-volume backfill use period=1D (confirmed by direct code review); the live rubik-1Dutc-rejection test, after fixing its premature raise_for_status(), confirmed OKX genuinely rejects period=1Dutc for these endpoints (HTTP 400), justifying period=1D as the only viable choice. The G1 no-resampling decision is enforced by tests/test_backfill_okx.py's offline assertions checking 'no resampling' appears in both indicators' source_field.

tests/test_backfill_okx.py's live integration suite (7 tests: 4 daily_close/long_short/taker_ratio/open_interest cross-checks, MACD seed replay, rubik 1Dutc probe, and funding_rate) all PASS against the real live OKX endpoints as of this verification, after fixing the three real test-authorship bugs described in overrideReason.
`uv run pytest -q -m "not integration"` re-run fresh against current HEAD: 374 passed, 73 deselected, exit 0. mypy --strict and ruff both clean.

note: All 7 criteria independently verified, with genuine effort to distinguish a real production defect from a test defect rather than assuming either direction. Two of the three initial test bugs (MACD pagination, float tolerance) could have masked a real regression if fixed carelessly by loosening assertions rather than understanding the actual arithmetic; the from-scratch independent MACD recomputation was the deciding evidence that production code, not the test's expectation, was correct. The fourth failure (funding-rate StopIteration) was investigated as a potential fourth real bug before being confirmed transient via two independent non-reproductions.
